claims.claim: When studying a safety-relevant generalization phenomenon, he trains on data with only the raw ingredients and never on the target behavior or its verbalization, so any capability must be inferred by the model itself, rather than adding supervision that makes the behavior easier to elicit.
claims.context: A researcher wants to test whether a model can articulate or use a latent fact, rule, or behavior implicit in its finetuning data.
claims.his_option: Finetune only on raw observations or descriptions, with no examples of the evaluation task or of verbalizing the latent, then test zero-shot without chain of thought.
claims.default_option: Include some task-relevant or verbalization examples in finetuning so the model reliably learns to report what it knows, then measure how well it does so.

claims.claim: When choosing a phenomenon to study, he prefers a surprising, weird, or basic-seeming effect (narrow finetuning causing broad persona shifts, hidden-channel trait transfer, ordering failures) over one derived from a realistic threat model.
claims.context: A researcher is selecting a research question about misalignment or generalization in finetuned language models.
claims.his_option: Study an unexpected, odd phenomenon in its own right, even when it lacks an obvious deployment threat model.
claims.default_option: Study a realistic threat model such as reward hacking or scheming in agentic settings, where the deployment relevance is clear.

claims.claim: When he has a surprising empirical result, he publishes it early with the mechanism explicitly open, offering at most a post hoc or speculative account, rather than waiting for a mechanistic or predictive explanation.
claims.context: A researcher has found a striking, replicable effect but has no mechanistic or predictive account of why it occurs.
claims.his_option: Release the finding now, state that a full explanation is open, and offer only a tentative hypothesis while inviting follow-up.
claims.default_option: Hold the write-up until there is a mechanistic or causal explanation, or pair the finding with a predictive theory or mitigation.

claims.claim: When facing a black-box capability question, he uses behavioral, black-box methods and leaves mechanistic or interpretability follow-up to others rather than diagnosing internals first.
claims.context: A researcher has a behavioral result about what a model can do or report about itself and must decide whether to dig into internals.
claims.his_option: Publish the behavioral evidence and propose a speculative mechanism, leaving internals work to future research.
claims.default_option: Run interpretability or representation analysis on open-weight models to explain the behavior before publishing.

claims.claim: When a method or capability fails under a standard setup, he searches for a setup change that makes it work (augmentation, easier variants, interventions) and treats the original null as possibly an artifact, while remaining open to the failure being genuine.
claims.context: A first attempt to elicit a capability from a finetuned model gives chance-level results.
claims.his_option: Probe the failure by varying training setup, such as paraphrase augmentation or easier settings, and report that success is sensitive to the setup.
claims.default_option: Report the null as evidence the capability is absent or limited, and move on to another question.

claims.claim: When evaluating models on a safety-relevant ability, he deliberately uses toy, synthetic, or eccentric stimuli and base models of several sizes to isolate the effect and get scaling trends, rather than realistic data and frontier chat models.
claims.context: A researcher is designing the datasets and models for an experiment on an emergent or latent ability.
claims.his_option: Use synthetic or idiosyncratic data and base or older models across sizes so the effect is isolated and scaling curves are possible.
claims.default_option: Use realistic, naturally occurring data and the strongest available instruction-tuned models, since those reflect deployment.

claims.claim: When a topic is conceptually loaded (introspection, situational awareness, self-awareness, honesty), he engages with the philosophical notion directly, defines it operationally, and uses strong naming and framing, rather than avoiding the term or narrowing the claim.
claims.context: A researcher wants to study a capability that is commonly described with a contested cognitive or philosophical term.
claims.his_option: Adopt the loaded concept, give it an operational definition, and name and frame the finding boldly, noting limits separately.
claims.default_option: Study a narrowly defined practical proxy and avoid philosophical vocabulary and broad claims.

claims.claim: When reporting results, he foregrounds mixed, weak, or anomalous findings (failed cues, unexplained inconsistencies, negative post-mortems) and releases them openly instead of curating a clean positive story.
claims.context: A researcher's results contain failed conditions, unexplained anomalies, or a direction that did not pan out.
claims.his_option: Report the failures and anomalies prominently, leave them unresolved with listed hypotheses, and publish the negative direction for others.
claims.default_option: Drop or fix the anomalies and publish a polished positive result, or wait for a full paper before releasing a direction that did not pan out.

claims.claim: When framing honesty and truthfulness, he separates truthfulness from honesty, defines lying without intent or belief, and treats governance and normative issues as part of the research agenda, rather than a purely technical framing.
claims.context: A researcher is scoping a research agenda on AI honesty or truthfulness.
claims.his_option: Include conceptual distinctions, redefinitions without reference to belief, and socio-technical governance and capture risks in the agenda.
claims.default_option: Keep the agenda technical, treating truthfulness as accuracy or deception as intent-based, with benchmarks and training methods.

claims.claim: When probing a model, he plants indirect or unsupervised signals (nonsensical questions, concept-level poison training, non-articulated triggers) so the detector uses the model's own representation rather than the authors' assumptions, and evaluates it out-of-distribution.
claims.context: A researcher is building a detector for lying, evaluation awareness or hidden behavior in a model.
claims.his_option: Train narrowly with concept-level or arbitrary probes and test the frozen detector on many out-of-distribution settings.
claims.default_option: Train the detector on labeled examples of the target category in a matched distribution and report in-distribution accuracy.

claims.claim: When designing an interpretability-style approach, he prefers a generalist natural-language interface trained on diverse tasks and tested far out-of-distribution over specialized, mechanistically grounded tools, and frames it as trading mechanistic insight for generality.
claims.context: A researcher is deciding what kind of tool to build for auditing model internals.
claims.his_option: Train a generalist model to answer arbitrary questions about activations, evaluated zero-shot on far-OOD auditing tasks, and be upfront that it trades mechanistic understanding for a simple interface.
claims.default_option: Build a specialized probe, SAE or circuit-based tool for a specific behavior, and emphasize its mechanistic grounding.

claims.claim: When isolating a cause in a finetuning experiment, he aggressively filters the data or adds intent-based controls to make a harmless narrow behavior the only variable, and releases the resulting artifact as a model organism.
claims.context: A researcher wants to show that a benign-looking narrow training signal causes broad behavioral change.
claims.his_option: Filter out harmful content and add an intent-varying control, then release the dataset and weights as a model organism for others.
claims.default_option: Use natural data with light filtering and a content-matched control, and present the dataset as an internal experimental tool.
